subject: How do I differentiate residual covariance from covariance of observed variables?

messages.author: 0b4ccab6b725eb7a
messages.subject: How do I differentiate residual covariance from covariance of observed variables?
parts:
Hi there,

I've been confused by this question for a while.

Suppose I'm running a path model of six observed variables:
pa.1<-' y3~y2+y1+x1+x2+x3
           y2~y1+x1+x2+x3
           y1~x1+x2+x3
           x1~~x2+x3
           x2~~x3'
summary(sem(pa.1,data=bp),fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE,rsquare=TRUE,modindices=TRUE)

Do I get the covariances of observed variables (x1-3) or the residual covariances between x1-3 in summary?
The possibility of x1-3 being correlated is acknowledged, but there is no interest in describing the causal dynamics between these three variables. How can I set them as unanalyzed relationships (linked with double-headed arrows) in my codes?

Thanks a lot!
O.S.

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: How do I differentiate residual covariance from covariance of observed variables?
parts: You will get the covariances between x1-x3 because they are predictors. You will not get residual covariances from predictors. However, by default, lavaan treats predictors like regression such that predictors are fixed variables. Thus, they do not estimate covariances between predictors in the model so distribution assumptions on predictors are not used. Lavaan reports covariances between predictors for convenience but not estimates the covariances in the model.

pa.1<-' y3~y2+y1+x1+x2+x3

           y1~x1+x2+x3

           x2~~x3

x1~z1+z2+z3
           x2~z1+z2+z3
           x3~z1+z2+z3'
summary(sem(pa.1,data=bp),fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE,rsquare=TRUE,modindices=TRUE)
The variables x1-3 are not only predictors of y1-3, but also outcomes of z1-3. Are they still treated as fixed variables?I hope my question makes sense. 

What intrigues me is, if I don't get it wrong, what happens with "~" in lavaan is very similar to what happens with "WITH" in Mplus.
When analyzing measurement models in Mplus, we use the command of "x1 WITH x2" to correlate the error terms of x1 and x2. 
However, when we want the correlation between x1 and x2 in path analysis, we also use the command of "x1 WITH x2" (http://www.ats.ucla.edu/stat/mplus/seminars/IntroMplus/path.htm).

Does that mean we are interpreting the residual correlations as covariances between observed variables? Can someone straighten the puzzle out?

Best regards,
O.S.

messages.author: e4a3215063481170
messages.subject: Re: Re: How do I differentiate residual covariance from covariance of observed variables?
parts:
hi O.S.

When you correlate two exogenous variables, you get their covariance. When you correlate two endogenous variables, it is the two residual variances that you are correlating, so it is the residual covariance. The exogenous variables are considered not influenced by other variables (although they actually are). The variances of the endogenous variables include roughly two parts, explained and unexplained variance. The explained variances of the endogenous variables are explained by the exogenous variables. The unexplained variances of the endogenous variables are residual (left unexplained) variances. So the covariance between exogenous variables (e.g., observed IV) are theoretically not the same thing as the residual covariance between endogenous variables (e.g., observed DV)

The operator "~" does not mean correlation, but regression. See the detail about operators in lavaan here: http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax1.html 

hope this help.

ya
